abstract: To achieve the goals of the Paris Agreement, substantial investments in clean energy are needed in developing countries. We study the challenges faced by developing countries in accessing financial resources for clean energy investments during the low-carbon transition in a dynamic stochastic general equilibrium model calibrated to Brazil. We show that financial frictions exacerbate the costs of the low-carbon transition and reduce the competitiveness in international capital markets with adverse effects on the inflow of foreign funds. In a policy analysis, we explore different revenue recycling schemes and highlight the advantages of combining carbon taxation with clean energy subsidies to attract foreign funds and accelerate clean capital accumulation. These results underscore the importance of considering financial market responses and international capital market integration in designing efficient climate policies for developing countries and provide a roadmap for policymakers to balance climate ambitions with macroeconomic stability and international competitiveness in emerging economies.
title: Financial frictions and climate policy in a small open economy

abstract: Old-age poverty is a growing concern in Sub-Saharan Africa, where pension coverage remains low, particularly in rural areas. Traditionally, older adults have relied on financial support from their children, but demographic and social changes are weakening this intergenerational contract. This study examines parents’ savings decisions within the framework of the intergenerational contract, focusing on the interaction between parental savings and child transfers in financing old-age security. Using a lab-in-the-field experiment with cocoa-farming households in rural Ghana, we analyze parental savings decisions, expectations of child support, and children’s transfer behavior. Our findings show that parents save substantial amounts regardless of expected or actual child transfers, and children do not adjust their contributions based on parental savings. We find no evidence of strategic under-saving or crowding out of private savings by expected future child transfers. The experimental results are consistent with elicited social norms that prescribe both parental savings and children’s financial support, pointing to an intergenerational contract based on shared responsibility rather than strategic substitution in rural Ghana. These findings suggest that in contexts with weak formal pensions, informal intergenerational contracts and private savings can coexist as complementary pillars of old-age security.
title: Balancing the Burden: Shared Responsibility in Intergenerational Financial Support in Rural Ghana

abstract: Post-disaster recovery is usually reported through aggregate budgets, obscuring which resources have reached an administratively consolidated stage, where they materialise, and which interventions operate beyond municipal boundaries. This study develops a reproducible ex post territorial audit of awarded public recovery investment after the 29 October 2024 floods in the Valencian Region, Spain. We reconcile 1647 procurement records closed on 28 February 2026 into published, awarded, municipally territorialised and non-municipalisable recovery states, and combine the municipal component with rainfall, flooded area, estimated affected population and water depth for 106 municipalities. Concentration measures, Moran’s I, Local Indicators of Spatial Association, Pearson and Spearman correlations, and a relative territorial adequacy indicator assess concentration, spatial clustering and proportional alignment without estimating causal allocation effects. Of EUR 3.241 billion published, EUR 1.454 billion had been awarded; EUR 1.157 billion was territorialised and EUR 297.42 million (20.45% of awards) remained non-municipalisable. Territorialised investment was highly concentrated (Gini = 0.763; top 15 municipalities = 72.57%) and spatially structured (Moran’s I = 0.420). It was more strongly associated with flooded area and estimated affected population than with rainfall. Among 66 municipalities retained for adequacy analysis, 23 were under-covered, 12 approximately proportional and 31 over-covered. The contribution is a scale-aware audit architecture that separates administrative recovery states and distinguishes concentration, clustering and alignment, preventing network-scale investment from being omitted or arbitrarily localised. The findings support georeferenced recovery registers, beneficiary-area coding and exposure-sensitive ex post review.
title: Auditing post-disaster recovery as land-use governance: Public investment after the 2024 floods in the Valencian Region, Spain

abstract: Civil wars are a recurring phenomenon undermining development in weak states. Faced with the possibility of costly conflict, why don’t leaders share power? I investigate the role of an unexplored commitment problem, both theoretically and empirically. The model features a leader who can appease challengers by sharing power, but doing so increases their effectiveness at launching a rebellion. I show that commitment worsens as the opposition becomes stronger, and derive testable non-monotonic implications of group strength on power-sharing and conflict. As challengers become stronger, the likelihood of inclusion (positive transfers) increases up to a threshold, beyond which the leader prefers to exclude an opposing group and face conflict. I test the model using data on politically relevant ethnic groups in Africa and Asia, their access to executive power, and on armed organizations that claim to represent them. I use within-country variation in population share to proxy for group strength. The empirical findings strongly accord with the predictions of the theory. I then structurally estimate the model parameters and explore policy-relevant counterfactuals, including the effects of democratization, changes in military capacity, financial aid, sanctions, and quotas.
journal: Journal of the European Economic Association
title: Conflict or Compromise? Theory and Evidence from Africa and Asia*

abstract: We examine whether designating banks as systemically important affects loan performance in an emerging-market setting where such banks are large domestic institutions and market imperfections make monitoring crucial for loan performance. Using loan-level data and the staggered designation of banks as Domestic Systemically Important Banks (DSIBs) in India, we find that loan performance deteriorates following DSIB designation. The evidence points to bank-level moral hazard as the underlying mechanism: DSIBs reduce postorigination monitoring and weaken loan recovery efforts. Borrowers respond accordingly, exhibiting poorer financial health and loan repayment, particularly on loans extended by DSIBs. This paper was accepted by Jan Bouwens, accounting. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.03238 .
publisher: Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS)
title: Systemically Important Banks and Loan Performance: Evidence from India

abstract: Identifying the cause of discrimination is crucial to designing effective policies and to understanding discrimination dynamics. This paper provides a potential link between existing models of taste-based and statistical discrimination by studying directional belief formation through biased information search and processing. By selectively acquiring and processing information, individuals form directional beliefs and consequently discriminate based on these beliefs. Through a series of experiments in which individuals endogenously acquire and process various signals, I document discrimination stemming from directional beliefs and demonstrate important differences in how it manifests compared with taste-based and statistical discrimination. Finally, I show that limiting individuals’ scope to interpret information reduces such discrimination. This paper was accepted by Marie Claire Villeval, behavioral economics and decision analysis. Funding: Financial support from the Sustainable Architecture for Finance in Europe Experiment Center Frankfurt [Grant 232406], the Interdisciplinary Public Policy Mainz [Grant A2021011], and the Mainzer Wissenschaftsstiftung is gratefully acknowledged. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.01818 .
publisher: Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS)
title: Why Do We Discriminate? Directional Beliefs and Biased Information Processing

abstract: We examine how different generations of artificial intelligence (AI) substitute for human knowledge worker tasks, leveraging two sequential natural experiments in the translation industry. We study the introduction of Google Neural Machine Translation (GNMT), a predictive, task-specific AI, as well as ChatGPT, a broad, general-purpose generative AI, in a major online labor market. Distinguishing between analytical tasks (regular translations) and intuitive tasks (transcreations, which require creative and cultural adaptation), we estimate difference-in-differences models on transaction-level data from 2016 to 2017 and 2022 to 2023. We find that GNMT reduced the demand for analytical tasks by economically meaningful magnitudes, while having no detectable effect on intuitive tasks. By contrast, ChatGPT produced substantially larger and more uniform reductions for both analytical and intuitive tasks, indicating a marked expansion in the scope and magnitude of AI substitution. By comparing these two technological shocks within the same labor market, we show that conclusions about which types of human work are resilient to automation do not straightforwardly generalize from predictive to generative AI. This paper was accepted by Joshua Gans, business strategy. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.06740 .
publisher: Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS)
title: AI-Driven Human Task Substitution: Evidence from Google Translate and ChatGPT

abstract: Using hourly data from January 2015 to September 2023, this study examines risk premia in the UK wholesale electricity market, focusing on market conditions, policy interventions, and geopolitical shocks. An hour-of-the-day panel analysis shows that negative prices became more frequent during low-demand early-morning hours and that risk premia are statistically significant across most hours, with the largest positive premia occurring between 19:00 and 22:00. Negative intraday and day-ahead prices, price spikes, and peak scarcity are the most robust correlates of the premium. The variables Brexit referendum, I-SEM coupling, Market Stability Reserve, formal Brexit exit, and EU acquis are associated with higher risk premia when estimated separately, although most coefficients become insignificant in joint specifications because the event indicators are sequentially correlated. The COVID-19 indicator is associated with a higher premium in the baseline specification, consistent with heightened uncertainty in short-horizon price formation. The Russia-Ukraine war is associated with a compression of the day-ahead premium relative to intraday prices, consistent with intraday prices increasing disproportionately during the war period. Extended specifications show positive coefficients for gas and carbon prices, and renewable generation. Core results are stable across estimators, subsamples and winsorisation, but are less robust to alternative premium definitions and narrow event windows. As the empirical design is reduced-form, the event coefficients are interpreted as conditional associations rather than causal effects. The study's findings highlight the importance of coordinated and stable policy design, improved renewable-generation forecasting and liquid intraday markets to manage short-horizon price risk while decarbonising the electricity sector.
title: Risk premia in the UK electricity market under policy uncertainty and market fragmentation

abstract: This paper examines whether aggregate shocks affect school participation uniformly across age groups. Using nationally representative NFHS-5 data from India, we draw on interrupted survey fieldwork around the 2020 school-closure period to compare children interviewed before and after the onset of pandemic-era schooling disruption within the same districts. School non-attendance was 1.3 percentage points higher after the disruption, equivalent to about 18 percent of the pre-disruption mean. The increase was concentrated among children aged 6–10, with the largest change among those aged 6–7, while children aged 11–14 showed no change. Reported reasons for non-attendance, together with time-use and labour-force evidence, are more consistent with delayed school entry, re-entry frictions, and weakened schooling routines than with full-time child labour or schooling-cost barriers. The findings indicate that pandemic-era schooling disruption was associated with weaker participation at foundational ages. Post-crisis recovery should therefore monitor early-grade entry, facilitate re-entry, and restore regular participation following major educational disruptions.
title: Aggregate Shocks and Foundational Schooling: Evidence from India

abstract: This paper examines the association between judges financial holdings and the outcome of legal cases. Using novel data on financial disclosures of judges and the civil case information of public firms across district courts in the United States between 2000 and 2021, we document multiple instances in which judges fail to recuse themselves from cases where they hold common stock in one of the parties. We find evidence that judges appear to rule more favorably when deciding over conflicted cases than when deciding over unconflicted ones. We also find that investors are positively surprised by these outcomes, as reflected by stock returns to case outcomes. The 2017 electronic disclosure reform, which made judicial financial holdings more accessible, significantly increases judges’ recusals and attenuates investor surprise. Collectively, our results provide the first large-scale evidence of the relation between judges’ financial holdings and case outcomes.
title: Judge financial holdings and case outcomes: Evidence from judge financial disclosures

abstract: Based on a comprehensive visual deception score constructed from China’s mandatorily disclosed IPO roadshow videos using computer vision and machine learning, we find that visual cues embedded in these videos predict IPO financial fraud. The predictive power is incremental to financial, textual, and audio indicators. Further analyses show that these cues are well grounded in psychology research and focusing on the psychology-based deception-cue-area features improves fraud predicting performance. Furthermore, decomposing each video into five topics, we find that only the deception score of the topic on financial performance is positively associated with financial fraud. We further show that insiders of firms with higher visual deception scores are more likely to sell shares shortly after lock-up periods expire, and these firms experience significantly lower subsequent stock returns. Our study demonstrates the feasibility and potential value of using video information for fraud detection in accounting and finance.

abstract: This paper examines whether and how environmental regulation affects firm-level market power, using China’s water pollutant emission intensity regulation in the paper industry as a natural experiment. Implemented in Shandong Province in 2003, the regulation required firms to reduce chemical oxygen demand intensity by one-third. We find that the policy significantly reduced market competition by inducing firm exit, leading surviving firms in Shandong to increase their markups by approximately 4.4% over the four years following implementation. The higher market power contributed to higher product prices charged by surviving firms.

abstract: We develop a model of employee mobility and wage formation suitable for analyzing labor market interventions that target wages and discrimination. By augmenting the standard asymmetric learning model with costly effort, wages are necessary for production and fully informative of employee ability, rather than products of public signals and employer competition, as in prior models. With salary disclosure, strategies to mask employee quality, common in standard models, are untenable; instead, the equilibrium has symmetric learning, optimal assignment, and efficient production. Salary history bans—policy in many jurisdictions—revert to asymmetric learning, with strategic under-assignment to manipulate noisy signals. Equal pay mandates that restrict intra-title wage variation, as may result from anti-discrimination law, prevent firms from fully utilizing employee skill. In the presence of discrimination, both salary history bans and equal pay mandates may result in reduced wage gaps, though at the expense of reduced production efficiency and returns to skill.
title: Wage signaling, salary history bans, and equality

abstract: I consider a neoclassical growth model with a constant absolute risk aversion (CARA) utility function and derive a global closed form approximation that is arbitrarily precise as the discount rate ρ is close to the population growth rate n . I use it to show that the consumption function is strictly concave and that countries can have two different paths converging to the steady-state: front-loading and back-loading.
title: An arbitrarily precise global closed form approximation for the neoclassical growth model

abstract: Causal mediation analysis typically assumes that all variables are fully observed, yet missingness is common and often nonignorable. We develop a framework for mediation analysis when pretreatment covariates, the mediator, and the outcome are all subject to missing not at random (MNAR). We propose three interpretable MNAR mechanisms, namely response continuation, self selection, and missingness driven by covariates and the mediator. Under each, we establish nonparametric identification of mediation effects using a shadow variable and completeness conditions. Empirical results show that subjective well-being partially mediates the association between job satisfaction and depressive symptoms.
title: Causal mediation analysis with nonignorable missingness in covariates, mediator, and outcome

abstract: Norway's hydropower reservoirs hold about 87 TWh of storage capacity, making them a potentially valuable resource for balancing variable renewable power in Northern Europe. Beyond existing resources, there are opportunities to expand hydropower generation and pumping capacity and increase cross-border transmission capacity. While several studies highlight system-level benefits of such developments, their distributional consequences have received less attention. Here, we use a stochastic power market optimization model to explore how Norwegian hydropower and cross-border transmission expansions, individually and combined, affect producers and consumers in scenarios for 2050. The model includes a simplified but integrated electricity-hydrogen sector coupling. Our results show substantial distributional effects: In the combined expansion scenario, revenues for wind and solar power producers increase in Norway and neighbouring countries, often by 5–20%. Consumer electricity prices decline by up to 3.6% in several continental European and UK regions but increase by 17–24% in southern Norway. Price volatility decreases in continental Europe and the UK (around 15% in several regions, based on standard-deviation metrics) while increasing in Norway. Overall, outcomes shift toward greater uniformity in both price levels and price volatility. System-wide operating costs fall by 5.5%, significantly more than the sum of reductions from hydropower expansion alone (0.38%) and transmission expansion alone (3.0%), indicating a synergy between the two developments. These results highlight the importance of transmission for unlocking the full flexibility benefits of Norwegian hydropower. The results show that system-wide benefits can coincide with substantial redistribution of costs and benefits across regions and stakeholder groups.
title: Redistribution effects of Norwegian hydropower and Norway-Europe transmission upgrades

abstract: We study the dynamics of the racial wealth gap (the wealth of Black households relative to white ones) using a dynamic equilibrium model of overlapping generations. We match the model to the cross‐sectional distributions of wealth and earnings by race. We find that equalizing earnings is critical for permanent reductions in racial wealth inequality, and that one‐time transfers will have only transitory effects unless earnings are also equalized. Our results are robust to the introduction of racial differences in returns to saving, which only matter after earnings inequality is reduced.
title: The Dynamics of the Racial Wealth Gap

abstract: We show that leading investor disagreement proxies have near-zero cross-correlation – making disagreement pricing inferences challenging. We develop a frictionless model that generates overpricing from latent disagreement, jointly rationalizes major proxies, and generates new testable predictions. Equilibrium interrelationships motivate a new disagreement measure, DIS, which is more predictive of returns cross-sectionally than major proxies and more consistently predictive across macroeconomic regimes. We provide evidence that the friction-based channel of Miller (1977) and a frictionless mechanism coexist and are empirically separable. DIS also provides a micro-founded, disagreement-based account of the IVOL puzzle, absorbing IVOL’s predictability while revealing its regime and friction dependence.
abstract_zh: 我们发现，主流投资者分歧代理变量之间的横截面相关性接近于零——这使得分歧定价推断颇具挑战。我们构建了一个无摩擦模型，该模型由潜在分歧产生高估定价，同时合理化了主要代理变量，并生成了新的可检验预测。均衡中的相互关系促使我们提出一个新的分歧度量指标DIS，其在横截面上对收益的预测能力优于主要代理变量，且在不同宏观经济体制下预测更为一致。我们提供证据表明，Miller（1977）基于摩擦的渠道与一种无摩擦机制并存，且在实证上可分离。DIS还为IVOL异象提供了一个具有微观基础、基于分歧的解释，吸收了IVOL的可预测性，同时揭示了其体制依赖性和摩擦依赖性。
title: Disagreement of disagreement

abstract: The symposium on reswitching, published sixty years ago in a special issue of the Quarterly Journal of Economics, represented a pivotal turning point in the debate on capital theory, known as the “Cambridge Controversy” due to the central roles of economists from Cambridge (UK) and Cambridge (Massachusetts). The passing of many key participants has led to the systematic opening of their personal archives, providing significant new opportunities for archival research. Drawing upon these newly accessible primary sources, this paper offers a comprehensive reconstruction of the special issue’s genesis, the questions it addressed, and the resolutions proposed. By elucidating the intellectual dynamics that shaped this fundamental debate, the paper argues that while the primary theoretical issues have largely been settled, several meta-theoretical questions remain open. Consequently, these archival findings remain highly relevant to the modern economic theorist.
abstract_zh: 六十年前发表在《经济学季刊》特刊上的关于再转换的研讨会，标志着资本理论辩论中的一个关键转折点，该辩论因来自剑桥（英国）和剑桥（马萨诸塞州）的经济学家所发挥的核心作用而被称为“剑桥之争”。许多关键参与者的逝世促使其个人档案被系统性地开放，为档案研究提供了重要的新机遇。本文依据这些新近可获取的一手资料，全面重构了该特刊的缘起、其所探讨的问题以及所提出的解决方案。通过阐明塑造这场根本性辩论的思想动态，本文认为，尽管主要的理论问题已在很大程度上得到解决，但若干元理论问题仍然悬而未决。因此，这些档案发现对现代经济理论家仍具有高度相关性。
title: The 1966 Special Issue of the QJE on Capital Theory and Reswitching A View from the Archives

abstract: In choice under risk, the curvature of Bernoulli utility function for money captures attitudes towards risk (under expected utility theory). Two popular functional forms for Bernoulli utility are an exponential function, which exhibits constant absolute risk aversion, and a power function, which exhibits constant relative risk aversion. Both struggle to capture a relatively high risk aversion over large stakes coexisting with a relatively low risk aversion over small stakes. This note presents a new utility function for money expressed via the modified Bessel function of the second kind that overcomes this problem. This utility function exhibits a constant coefficient xu(x)’’/u(x).
abstract_zh: 在风险选择中，货币伯努利效用函数的曲率（在期望效用理论下）体现了风险态度。两种流行的伯努利效用函数形式是指数函数，其表现出恒定绝对风险厌恶，以及幂函数，其表现出恒定相对风险厌恶。二者都难以刻画在大额赌注上相对较高的风险厌恶与在小额赌注上相对较低的风险厌恶并存的情况。本文提出了一种通过第二类修正贝塞尔函数表示的新的货币效用函数，克服了这一问题。该效用函数表现出恒定系数 xu(x)’’/u(x)。
title: On Utility Functions for Money

abstract: Whether recurrent flood exposure deters demand for flood-exposed urban land, a deterrence logic well established in mature Anglo-American property markets, is a growing consideration for land-use planning under climate change. This question travels poorly to dense, platform-mediated Chinese urban housing markets, where households face repeated flooding at first hand while statutory hazard disclosure remains comparatively thin. Drawing on a pan-Chinese survey of 505 urban residents across 29 provinces, with 52 % in the coastal high-flood-risk belt, this paper develops and tests a structural model of housing purchase intention under urban flood risk. The model integrates a loss-normalisation block (perceived loss tolerability, investment discounting), a risk-cognition block (perceived flood risk, flood-information salience) and the proximal theory of planned behaviour. Covariance-based structural equation modelling yields three findings consequential for land-use planning. First, perceived loss tolerability raises purchase intention directly, while investment discounting raises it through attitude, so that both absorb the flood-risk signal rather than transmitting deterrence. Second, recurrent-event habituation and optimism bias depress perceived risk and feed both mechanisms, giving the levee effect a micro-level foundation. Third, the attitude-to-intention path is not significant, with subjective norm dominating intention, and objective flood knowledge does not moderate these effects. Taken together, the results suggest that demand-side responses alone are unlikely to steer development away from flood-exposed urban land, which points to a larger role for planning in risk-sensitive land allocation.
abstract_zh: 反复暴露于洪水是否会抑制对洪水易发城市土地的需求，这一在成熟英美房地产市场中已充分确立的威慑逻辑，正日益成为气候变化下土地利用规划的重要考量。然而，该问题难以直接移植到密集的、平台中介的中国城市住房市场，因为家庭虽亲身经历反复洪水，但法定灾害信息披露仍相对薄弱。本文基于一项覆盖中国29个省份505名城市居民的全国性调查（其中52%位于沿海高洪水风险带），构建并检验了城市洪水风险下购房意愿的结构模型。该模型整合了损失正常化模块（感知损失可容忍性、投资折价）、风险认知模块（感知洪水风险、洪水信息显著性）以及近端计划行为理论。基于协方差的结构方程建模得出三项对土地利用规划具有重要意义的发现。第一，感知损失可容忍性直接提高购房意愿，而投资折价通过态度提高购房意愿，因此二者均吸收洪水风险信号而非传递威慑效应。第二，反复事件习惯化与乐观偏差压低感知风险并助推上述两种机制，从而为堤坝效应提供了微观基础。第三，态度至意愿的路径不显著，主观规范主导意愿，且客观洪水知识并未调节这些效应。综合来看，结果表明仅靠需求侧反应不太可能引导开发远离洪水易发城市土地，这指向规划在风险敏感型土地配置中发挥更大作用。

abstract: We develop a model to study the efficiency of socially responsible investing (SRI) as a mechanism to control firms' externalities. When SRI is not too popular, responsible investors favor strategies that lead to a concentration of SRI in a subset of firms in the economy. This concentration can mitigate coordination issues in adopting green technologies, but it can also crowd out the green investments of excluded firms and increase the price of green products. In equilibrium, responsible investors continue to favor concentration even as SRI becomes more popular, and concentrate the most when concentration is least desirable.
abstract_zh: 我们构建了一个模型，旨在研究社会责任投资（SRI）作为控制企业外部性机制的有效性。当SRI尚未过于普及时，负责任投资者倾向于采取那些导致SRI在经济中部分企业集中的策略。这种集中虽能缓解采用绿色技术时的协调难题，但也可能挤出被排除在外企业的绿色投资，并推高绿色产品的价格。在均衡状态下，即便SRI日益流行，负责任投资者仍偏好集中策略，并且在集中最不可取时反而集中程度最高。

abstract: Developing countries face critical tensions between farmland-use policies prioritizing food security and environmental sustainability, and farmers’ livelihood-centered land-use strategies. To address these challenges, this study develops a human-centered agent-based model that integrates dual-layer Q-learning with GIS-based spatial representation. This framework simulates farmers’ adaptive decision-making under dynamic policy and environmental conditions while formalizing behavioral heterogeneity through Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB)-informed typologies. Agents dynamically evolve land-transfer and cropping strategies via perception–action–feedback learning cycles. Applied to and validated against empirical observations from a representative Chinese case, the model reveals non-linear scale–efficiency relationships, with medium-scale farms exhibiting the comparatively balanced performance across yield and multiple resource-use efficiency dimensions. The analysis further identifies evolutionary pathways of adaptive behavior under policy incentives and quantifies trade-offs among area-weighted crop output, resource-use efficiency, and regional gross income. Scenario simulations show that rice-oriented subsidies increase rice output but reduce resource-use efficiency, rapeseed output, and gross income, whereas rotation-oriented incentives increase gross income while maintaining rice output near the baseline level. These findings support performance-linked subsidies based on multidimensional outcomes, tiered land-transfer regulation, and diversified cropping incentives. By linking adaptive behavioral dynamics with spatial and institutional constraints, this study provides a robust analytical framework for evaluating land-use policies and supports more effective governance strategies for balancing food security, environmental sustainability, and rural livelihoods.
abstract_zh: 发展中国家面临着优先保障粮食安全和环境可持续性的农田利用政策与以农民生计为中心的土地利用策略之间的关键矛盾。为应对这些挑战，本研究开发了一个以人为中心的基于主体的模型，将双层Q学习与基于GIS的空间表征相结合。该框架模拟了农民在动态政策和环境条件下的适应性决策，同时通过基于计划行为理论（TPB）的类型学将行为异质性形式化。主体通过感知—行动—反馈学习循环动态演化土地流转和种植策略。将该模型应用于中国一个代表性案例并与实证观测结果进行验证，结果揭示了非线性的规模—效率关系，其中中等规模农场在产量和多个资源利用效率维度上表现出相对均衡的绩效。分析进一步识别了政策激励下适应性行为的演化路径，并量化了面积加权作物产出、资源利用效率和区域总收入之间的权衡。情景模拟表明，以水稻为导向的补贴增加了水稻产出，但降低了资源利用效率、油菜籽产出和总收入，而以轮作为导向的激励措施在将水稻产出维持在基线水平附近的同时增加了总收入。这些发现支持基于多维结果的绩效挂钩补贴、分级土地流转监管和多元化种植激励。通过将适应性行为动态与空间和制度约束相联系，本研究为评估土地利用政策提供了一个稳健的分析框架，并支持更有效的治理策略，以平衡粮食安全、环境可持续性和农村生计。
china_relevance_reason: 论文以中国代表性案例进行实证验证，研究对象为中国农户土地利用决策与政策设计，属于中国研究。
title: From rules to learning: A GIS-integrated agent-based reinforcement learning framework for simulating farmers’ land-use decisions and sustainable policy design
title_zh: 从规则到学习：一种集成GIS的基于智能体的强化学习框架，用于模拟农户土地利用决策与可持续政策设计

abstract: Several countries are working to interlink their domestic fast payment systems in order to reduce costs and improve the speed and transparency of cross-border payments. This column presents econometric evidence suggesting that countries with interlinked systems trade with each other about 4% more than countries that lack such interlinkages. The trade gains are larger in regions with high cross-border payment costs and for systems that allow the settlement of wholesale transactions.
abstract_zh: 一些国家正在努力将其国内快速支付系统互联互通，以降低成本并提高跨境支付的速度和透明度。本专栏提出的计量经济学证据表明，拥有互联互通系统的国家之间的贸易额比缺乏此类互联互通的国家高出约4%。在跨境支付成本较高的地区以及允许批发交易结算的系统，贸易收益更大。
authors: Massimo Ferrari Minesso, Laura Lebastard, Olga Triay Bagur
china_relevance_reason: 研究主题为支付系统互联与跨境贸易，属跨国一般性研究，未以中国为研究对象、数据或制度背景。
title: Connecting payment systems, linking economies
title_zh: 连接支付系统，联通经济体

abstract: The expansion of artificial intelligence has triggered a surge of investment and rising equity values at technology firms. The largest firms, known as ‘hyperscalers’, issued over $100 billion of bonds in 2025, around five times the 2023-2024 annual average. This column compares bond yields for hyperscalers and other firms, before and after ChatGPT’s release in 2022. Hyperscalers’ yields fell by about 29 basis points relative to other firms, and by 42 basis points relative to software firms, whose business models artificial intelligence may disrupt. As hyperscalers’ debt grows, it remains critical to monitor whether these pricing effects continue.
abstract_zh: 人工智能的扩张引发了科技公司投资激增与股权价值上升。被称为“超大规模企业”的最大型公司于2025年发行了超过1000亿美元的债券，约为2023—2024年年均水平的五倍。本专栏比较了超大规模企业与其他企业在2022年ChatGPT发布前后的债券收益率。超大规模企业的收益率相对于其他企业下降了约29个基点，相对于商业模式可能被人工智能颠覆的软件企业下降了42个基点。随着超大规模企业债务的增长，持续监测这些定价效应是否延续仍至关重要。
title: Financing the AI boom: Winners and losers in corporate bond markets
title_zh: 为人工智能热潮融资：公司债券市场中的赢家与输家

abstract: This paper introduces a ranking over opportunity sets based on preferences satisficing: a set satisfices a preference if and only if there exists an element in the set that is considered good enough to meet the preference, and sets are ranked by the number of satisficed preferences. I compare this framework with existing models of ranking over sets and show that, when preferences are not exogenously given, it is characterized by two axioms identical to those in Kreps (1979), who analyzed rankings over sets from the perspective of preferences maximization. This result indicates that we cannot distinguish whether the ranking over sets is generated according to preferences maximization or preferences satisficing.
abstract_zh: 本文引入了一种基于偏好满足的机会集排序：一个集合满足某一偏好，当且仅当该集合中存在一个被认为足够好以满足该偏好的元素，而集合则根据被满足偏好的数量进行排序。我将这一框架与现有的集合排序模型进行比较，并表明，当偏好并非外生给定之时，该框架可由与Kreps（1979）中相同的两条公理加以刻画；Kreps从偏好最大化的视角分析了集合排序。这一结果表明，我们无法区分集合排序究竟是依据偏好最大化还是偏好满足生成的。
title: Diversity in opportunity sets: perspective from preferences satisficing
title_zh: 机会集的多样性：偏好满足的视角

abstract: How should monetary policy respond to climate policy shocks? We develop an Environmental New-Keynesian model with green and fossil energy to assess the macroeconomic impacts of carbon pricing and green subsidy shocks and to identify the optimal monetary policy responses. Our findings indicate that these shocks create a policy trade-off between stabilizing inflation and the output gap. This trade-off is resolved in favor of output-gap stabilization, with optimal monetary policy focusing on dampening real output fluctuations while temporarily looking through inflation movements. Dual mandate Taylor rules yield lower welfare costs than inflation-only targeting rules and align the welfare performances of core and headline inflation targeting regimes.
authors: Marco Carli & Francesca Diluiso & Mathias Hoffmann
title: Navigating climate policy shocks: optimal monetary policy responses

abstract: The fiscal transfers deployed during the COVID-19 pandemic were unprecedented in scale and strongly progressive. Using CPS/ASEC data, we document that the decline in employment during the pandemic was larger for low-income households and tightly linked to the intensity of transfer receipt, a pattern absent during the Global Financial Crisis. We develop and estimate a two-sector, heterogeneous-household general equilibrium model in which low-income households are borrowing-constrained in normal times but can save out of sufficiently large transfers. Because preferences permit wealth effects on labor supply, transfers both reduce labor supply and raise consumption, and a dollar of transfers is split roughly evenly between the two margins. We find that the effects of transfers are state-dependent: because the borrowing constraint binds more tightly in a deeper recession, the same transfer relaxes a tighter constraint and delivers an employment and consumption response about 40 to 50 percent larger during the pandemic than when the same transfer is introduced in the steady state. In the model, transfers were welfare-improving for recipients, with gains diminishing as transfers increase.
title: A Macroeconomic Analysis of Household Labor Supply Responses to Large Fiscal Transfers
